title: RayX Reactive Complexity, Concurrency, and Allocation Optimization

scope.problem: The new rayx_reactive and rayx_reactive_primitives crates expose a broad API that must remain available, while current Signal, Computed, activation, stream, delivery, and GPUI paths contain correctness-sensitive startup gaps plus avoidable locking, cloning, Arc ownership, and payload transport.
scope.outcome: Both reactive crates retain their complete public surface, deterministic concurrent and reentrant behavior is proven, redundant work is removed by direct operation evidence, and apps/test_suite proves the final public API on native and headed WASM/WebGPU runtimes.
inScope: Preserve every current public item in rayx_reactive, rayx_reactive_primitives, the rayx::reactive module, and the RayX prelude.
Make Signal mutation and values subscription lossless and version ordered under concurrent and reentrant use.
Make Computed construction lossless while user derivation closures execute outside internal coordinator mutexes.
Make activation callbacks lock-safe and simplify DisposeBag ownership without changing its API.
Remove directly proven redundant clone, Arc, mutex, and Clone-bound work from stream operators, DeliveryQueue, Signal forwarding, and GPUI bindings.
Record before/after Criterion evidence and exact clone/non-Clone evidence.
Add a public-API reactive fixture to apps/test_suite with native DevKit/MCP and headed WASM/WebGPU Playwright proof.
Update narrow RayX skill guidance and durable AgentX reactive-state memory after implementation evidence exists.
outOfScope: Deleting, renaming, hiding, deprecating, or replacing any current public API because it lacks present call sites.
Adding derive macros, batching, coalescing, backpressure, caches, custom allocators, unsafe code, or a new concurrency framework.
Changing EventBus, Command, AsyncCommand, Effect, or reactive collection semantics beyond downstream regression validation.
Using apps/lab or tools-node/lab for diagnostics, runtime proof, automation, probes, fixtures, or performance measurement.
Adopting behavior from an external implementation.

compatibility: All current direct-crate and umbrella-crate reactive imports MUST remain source-compatible.
Ordering, duplicates, equality suppression, errors, subscription lifetime, and side effects MUST remain unchanged except for the explicit losslessness and lock-safety corrections.
publicApi: No current public type, trait, method, function, alias, module export, or prelude export is deleted, renamed, hidden, deprecated, or replaced.
Lack of current call sites is not evidence that a public API is removable.
No new public API is introduced unless a later explicit user decision changes this epic.
dependencies: rayx_reactive MUST continue depending on rayx_reactive_primitives and MUST NOT depend on rayx_reactive_collections.
No production dependency is added; Criterion 0.5.1 is the only planned dev-dependency addition.
data: No persisted schema, protocol, network payload, file format, or migration is introduced.
SignalChange previous/current/version payload semantics remain stable.
operations: apps/test_suite is the exclusive application for native, WASM, Android, DevKit/MCP, Playwright, diagnostics, probes, and performance validation.
Playwright specifications MUST live under tools-node/test_suite.
apps/lab and tools-node/lab are forbidden diagnostic and automation targets.

functionalRequirements.title: Linearizable signal mutation and subscription
functionalRequirements.statement: Signal mutation and values subscription MUST form one ordered versioned contract: equal concurrent set calls commit at most one transition, committed mutations deliver in version order, and a values subscriber receives one synchronous snapshot followed by every later committed version.

evidence.reason: Current state, version assignment, DeliveryQueue forwarding, and values startup are owned here.

behavior.trigger: A caller invokes set, replace, update, changes, or values on shared Signal handles.
inputs: The current value/version, a replacement value or update closure, and current subscribers.
outputs: The existing Result and SignalChange values plus ordered subscriber callbacks.
stateChanges: A successful mutation commits one value and one monotonically advanced nonzero version.
values installs a subscriber and emits one synchronous current snapshot.
invariants: Equality suppression and mutation are one atomic decision.
Callbacks run without the Signal state coordinator mutex.
No committed version after the subscriber baseline is lost or duplicated.
errors: A poisoned internal mutex returns ReactiveError::Poisoned through the existing Result surface.
edgeCases: Reentrant mutation from the synchronous values callback.
Version wrap preserves the existing nonzero version rule.

evidence.reason: Current derive/combine startup, latest-pair mutex, and DisposeBag ownership are implemented here.

inputs: One or two ReadSignal sources and a user derivation or combination closure.
outputs: A Computed value whose values and changes retain the existing public semantics.
stateChanges: Construction captures source versions and installs owned subscriptions.
Later source versions update the computed Signal exactly through the existing output surface.
invariants: User code executes outside internal source and latest-value mutexes.
Construction does not lose versions committed after its baseline.
Dropping Computed drops its source subscriptions.
errors: Existing source or subscription errors are returned through ReactiveError.
Failed internal output replacement is not converted into a public API change.
edgeCases: Computed drops during later source activity.

functionalRequirements.title: Lock-safe activation and disposal
functionalRequirements.statement: ViewModelActivator and DisposeBag MUST preserve their complete public surface while activation callbacks execute outside activator locks, concurrent activation scopes dispose exactly once, failed activation leaves no live scope, and DisposeBag stores subscriptions without a redundant internal Arc.

evidence.reason: Current callback registration, active count, failure cleanup, and active bag lifecycle are implemented here.

behavior.trigger: A caller registers when_activated callbacks, activates one or more tokens, drops tokens, or disposes a DisposeBag.
inputs: Activation callbacks, ActivationToken lifetimes, Subscription values, and callback Results.
outputs: The existing Result, ActivationToken, disposed subscriptions, and is_disposed state.
stateChanges: First activation creates one generation bag.
Concurrent tokens share the generation count.
Final token drop or callback failure detaches and disposes the generation once.
invariants: Activation callbacks execute without the activator state mutex.
A failed generation cannot dispose a later generation.
errors: A callback error disposes partial work and returns the original error.
Poisoning follows the existing ReactiveError behavior.

functionalRequirements.title: Lean lossless GPUI transport
functionalRequirements.statement: ReactiveContextExt MUST preserve lossless ordered foreground delivery while bind_stream_value owns the futures unbounded sender directly, notify_on transports unit notifications without cloning payloads, and apps/test_suite proves binding lifetime and UI notification behavior.

evidence.reason: Current sender wrapping, payload cloning, foreground task, and GpuiBinding lifetime are implemented here.

behavior.trigger: A GPUI entity binds or notifies from a ValueStream and the stream emits values.
inputs: A ValueStream, entity Context, on_value callback, payloads, and binding lifetime.
outputs: Ordered foreground entity updates or notifications through the existing GpuiBinding API.
stateChanges: The binding owns one subscription and one foreground receive task.
Dropping the binding ends its subscription lifetime.
invariants: bind_stream_value preserves one ordered foreground application per received value.
notify_on transports unit and performs zero payload clones.
No GPUI entity API is called from the subscriber thread.
errors: Entity update failure terminates the receive loop without retry.

risks: A subscription handshake that is correct for simple concurrency can still fail under reentrant initial callbacks; the controlled regression is mandatory.
Activation failure can race a later generation; generation identity and exactly-once disposal evidence are mandatory.
Criterion noise can obscure a regression; only one predefined twice-duration rerun is accepted.
An overly broad final repair can cross sprint ownership; convergence blocks and routes repairs back to the owning task.
deferredNonGoals: Reactive derive macros and broader API sugar.
Stream backpressure, batching, coalescing, caches, pooling, custom allocation, SIMD, and unsafe code.
A combined scalar and SourceList/SourceCache demonstration beyond the focused scalar Test Suite fixture.
Android runtime proof because the internal optimization is target-agnostic and the required observable slice is explicitly native plus WASM; Android remains a later validation expansion.
